scope: 20 of 36 exact Babylon screenshots inspected. Static frozen-weight diagnostic only; no animation, anatomical rhythm or production qualification.
observations: Legacy shoulder 45 rotates from an abducted rest direction; it differs from the explicit sagittal 45 target by approximately 24.05 degrees. This is a test-definition mismatch, not proof of a faulty game animation.
World-target shoulder poses reach the intended directions, but 90-degree shoulder compression and the flattened transition into the upper arm remain visible at orbits 1 and 3.

The authored 15-degree clavicle control shifts the shoulder centre and rounds its outer silhouette somewhat; it does not establish acceptable shoulder anatomy or remove the abrupt upper-arm transition.
Both exact 90-degree hip targets retain the deep upper-thigh/groin crease. Outer-hip views also retain abrupt waist/hip transitions.
Adding 60 degrees of knee flexion changes the thigh silhouette, but does not visibly resolve the hip-root crease. The pelvis and hip direction remain fixed.

The 90-degree legacy direction errors are small (about 3.13 shoulder and 0.85 hip degrees). Correcting direction and adding these authored controls do not explain away the persistent deep-bend defects.
decision: Do not fit or publish this dense field. Use explicit measured directions in new comparisons; preserve historical isolated tests unchanged.
next_requirement: Define an explicit desired shoulder/hip surface for the measured poses and validate a localized shape repair against independent views and held-out motion. If no credible target can be authored, obtain a technical-art shape pass rather than tune the same proxy again.
